title: Small-World Den Building
strapline: Twigs, moss and pebbles become a home for the fairies, the dinosaurs, the tiny bears.
intent: Children build miniature homes, dens and worlds for small-world figures, merging construction with rich imaginative play.
Children plan and problem-solve at small scale — how to make a roof, a wall, a bridge that holds.
Children develop fine-motor control placing, balancing and joining tiny natural and made materials.
Children tell stories and take on characters as their small worlds come alive.
Children explore ideas of home, habitat and belonging through the shelters they build.
implementation: Offer a tray or corner with natural loose parts — twigs, moss, bark, pebbles, leaves, cones — and small-world figures.
Add joining and building bits — clay or dough as a base, string, small blocks, fabric scraps.
Follow the children's stories: who is this den for, what do they need, who is coming to visit?
Model the building language — wall, roof, doorway, cosy, shelter, strong enough — as you play alongside.
Support problem-solving gently when a roof collapses: 'what could hold that up?'
Link to habitats and stories — a home for a woodland creature, a cave for a dragon, a nest for a bird.
Photograph the finished worlds and let stories carry across days as dens are rebuilt and changed.
key_questions: Who is this home for? What will they need?
How can you make a roof that stays up?
What could you use for a soft, cosy bed?
How will they get in and out?
What happens in your little world?

impact.text: Children build small structures and homes with natural materials.
Children plan and solve small-scale construction problems.
Children place and balance tiny parts with fine-motor control.
Children tell stories and take on characters in their world.
Children explore ideas of home, habitat and belonging.
Children stay deeply absorbed, extending their world over time.

enhancements: Themed figure sets — woodland animals, dinosaurs, fairies, dragons.
Clay or dough as a base to press twigs and stones into.
A tuff tray with soil, moss and water for a living small world.
Fabric scraps, wool and cotton wool for cosy interiors.
A camera to photograph and revisit the worlds.
Books about homes and habitats to spark ideas.

playing_exploring: Children explore natural materials and what they can become.
They build and rebuild their worlds, following their stories.
active_learning: Children stay absorbed, developing a world across days.
They persist to make a roof or wall that holds.
creating_thinking: Children imagine a home and plan how to build it.
They solve construction problems and weave stories as they build.
